# Incident Report — 2024-08-15 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim host
| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.8.15.133 | Consistent source of all suspicious traffic; leases DHCP twice (.132 then .133) |
| MAC | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 | ARP resolution for 10.8.15.133; matches DHCP client-id in requests |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV | DHCP option 12, NBNS name registration, Kerberos CNameString |
| Domain | LAFONTAINEBLEU.ORG (NetBIOS: LAFONTAINEBLEU) | Kerberos realm, DHCP domain-name option, NBNS |
| Logged-in user | plucero | Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString from 10.8.15.133 to DC 10.8.15.4 |

The LAN is 10.8.15.0/24, gateway 10.8.15.1 (00:16:9c:02:a7:4b), domain controller 10.8.15.4 (WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org).

## Malware family
**Latrodectus** loader — **attribution: behavioral**, not signature-confirmed (no IDS/Suricata alerts were provided with this evidence set; conclusion is based solely on TTPs observed in the pcap).

Basis for the call:
- Delivery via a fake-invoice/parcel-tracking themed site (`quote.checkfedexexp.com`) serving a ZIP containing a single oversized `.js` file (~6.99 MB), padded with large blocks of irrelevant text (academic/report text) purely to inflate size and evade AV — a known Latrodectus/IcedID-lineage packaging technique.
- That JS dropper triggers a follow-on download of a PE32+ x86-64 DLL from a bare-IP host over plain HTTP (`72.5.43.29`), consistent with the loader being retrieved for execution via `rundll32.exe`.
- The DLL response is deliberately mislabeled `Content-Type: text/html` despite serving a raw PE binary — evasion behavior.
- Post-execution, the host beacons to that same bare IP roughly every 5–10 seconds with `GET /` using an anachronistic, static `User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` — over 300 beacons spanning the full remainder of the capture (~30 minutes) — interspersed with `POST /` requests carrying hex-encoded binary payloads (one exfil POST ~305 KB), matching the C2 checkin/exfil pattern documented for Latrodectus.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — TCP/HTTP C2. First contact at t+135.9s (DLL retrieval), then 300+ periodic `GET /` beacons with the fixed MSIE 6.0 user-agent and 3 `POST /` exfil requests through the end of the capture (t+1962s).

**Malicious domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` — fake FedEx-themed lure domain, resolved to 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159 (Cloudflare-fronted). Delivery-chain host.
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` — same lure infrastructure; DNS query observed (10.8.15.4 → resolved to 172.67.170.159 / 104.21.55.70) but no HTTP request followed in this capture.

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — GET at t+74.7s, returned a 200 OK, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `Server: cloudflare`, delivering the malicious ZIP (2,767,804 bytes).
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — HEAD then GET at t+135.9s, returned 200 OK, `Content-Length: 159232` (mislabeled `text/html`), delivering the DLL payload.

**Transferred files / hashes**
| File | SHA256 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| ZIP archive (from `/managements?...`) | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` | 2,767,804 bytes, deflate |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (inside ZIP) | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` | 6,990,020 bytes, padded with junk text; JS dropper |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (from `72.5.43.29/data/`) | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` | 159,232 bytes, PE32+ DLL (x86-64) — the loader payload |

## Benign context (not IOCs)
Cloudflare edge IPs 104.21.55.70 and 172.67.170.159 (CDN fronting only, not malicious themselves — the abuse is the domain, not the IP). All Microsoft/Windows/Bing/Edge telemetry, WU/BITS delivery (`msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`, `fe3cr.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`), Office/OneDrive endpoints, SSDP/mDNS/LLMNR local discovery, AD/Kerberos/LDAP/DCERPC domain traffic to 10.8.15.4, and NCSI connectivity checks (`www.msftconnecttest.com`) are normal enterprise/OS background noise.

## Incident summary
DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133, MAC 00:1c:bf:03:54:82), logged in as domain user `plucero` (LAFONTAINEBLEU.ORG), visited a fake FedEx-themed page at `quote.checkfedexexp.com` and downloaded a ZIP containing a padded, oversized JavaScript dropper. That dropper retrieved and executed a PE32+ DLL loader from a bare IP (72.5.43.29) over plain HTTP, after which the host established persistent C2 beaconing to `72.5.43.29:80` for the remainder of the capture (~30 minutes, 300+ checkins plus data exfil POSTs) — behavior consistent with the Latrodectus malware family, though attribution here is behavioral rather than signature-confirmed since no IDS alert export accompanied this evidence.
